sanctioned(a08).

% Check criterion: age >= 21
age_ok(A) :- applicant(A, Age, _, _), Age >= 21.

% Check criterion: residency_years >= 3
residency_ok(A) :- applicant(A, _, _, ResYears), ResYears >= 3.

% Check criterion: no sanction
no_sanction_ok(A) :- applicant(A, _, _, _), not sanctioned(A).

% Applicants with missing income
missing_income(A) :- applicant(A, _, Income, _), Income is absent.

% Applicants where all non-income criteria are met
other_criteria_met(A) :- age_ok(A), residency_ok(A), no_sanction_ok(A).

% Find applicants where missing income is the only barrier
answer(A) :- missing_income(A), other_criteria_met(A).

% A person can work a shift if:
% 1. They are qualified for the shift's role
% 2. They are NOT listed as unavailable for that shift
can_work(Person, Shift) :-
    shift(Shift, Role),
    qualified(Person, Role),
    not unavailable(Person, Shift).

% A shift can be worked if at least one person can work it
shift_can_be_worked(Shift) :- can_work(_, Shift).

% Find shifts where nobody can work
answer(Shift) :- shift(Shift, _), not shift_can_be_worked(Shift).

% Import data from CSV files
import "shift.csv" as shift.
import "qualified.csv" as qualified.
import "unavailable.csv" as unavailable.
import "assignment.csv" as assignment.

% Define shift time data more explicitly for overlap checking
% shift_info(id, role, start_str, end_str)
shift_info(ID, Role, Start, End) :- shift(id: ID, role: Role, start: Start, end: End).

% Check if two time strings overlap (using string comparison on ISO 8601 timestamps)
% Shift1 overlaps Shift2 if start1 < end2 AND start2 < end1
overlaps(S1, S2) :-
  shift_info(S1, _, Start1, End1),
  shift_info(S2, _, Start2, End2),
  S1 != S2,
  Start1 < End2,
  Start2 < End1.

% Check if a person has an assignment that overlaps with a given shift
has_overlapping_assignment(Person, Shift) :-
  assignment(person: Person, shift: AssignedShift),
  overlaps(Shift, AssignedShift).

% Check if a person can work a shift
can_work(Person, Shift) :-
  shift_info(Shift, Role, _, _),
  qualified(person: Person, role: Role),
  not unavailable(person: Person, shift: Shift),
  not has_overlapping_assignment(Person, Shift).

% Count how many people can work each shift
num_can_work(Shift, N) :-
  shift_info(Shift, _, _, _),
  N = count { P | can_work(P, Shift) }.

% Find shifts with exactly one person who can work them
answer(Shift, Person) :-
  num_can_work(Shift, 1),
  can_work(Person, Shift).
